newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end up sharply, near new contract highs.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end up sharply, near new contract highs.

text.p: CME lean hog futures held sharp gains at the close after posting new contract highs on demand sparked by strong fundamental and technical factors, traders said. Pork bellies were also up on firmer cash belly prices and late fund buying, traders said.

Hogs closed 1.225 to 0.175 cent per lb higher with April up most and June up 1.025 at 82.650 cents. Nearby June and July, as well as distant June and July, posted new contract highs with nearby June setting a new high of 82.900 cents and July at 82.450 cents. Pork bellies finished 1.125 cent per lb higher to unchanged with May up 1.075 at 82.350 cents.
Higher cash pork prices and gains in cash hog prices Thursday as well as calls for higher cash markets again Friday prompted commercial demand in hog futures, traders said.
"Most people want to feel that we cleaned up the pork and have it on a firmer tone and that's encouraging" strength in futures, said Bob VandeVorde with Farmers Marketing Resources.

VandeVorde also said the strength in cash hogs is a combination of seasonally tighter hog supplies and short-term weather effects. The lean hog index keeps going up which should push the April contract higher, he said.
Packers actively vied for hogs Thursday and talk circulate that cash hogs would climb another $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt Friday, floor sources said.
Further bolstering hog futures, especially summer months, was the Taiwan pork ban and the expected increased demand from Japan for U.S. pork.
"Exports we will have to (Japan) is going to be a nice solid supporting influence for us - giving up price levels we wouldn't have before," VandeVorde added.
The Dutch swine fever problem was further compounding bullish ideas, sources said.
The Dutch Farm Ministry on Thursday said it planned extra measures to control a swine fever epidemic in the south of the Netherlands that has so far lead to the slaughter of some 650,000 pigs.

R.J. O'Brien, Rand Financials, FIMAT Futures USA, Refco, KASA and Smith Barney were all cited as buyers in June hogs. Lind-Waldock and LFG sold early. Short covering was general in April, especially ahead of its expiration on Monday and no trading limits starting Friday, pit sources said.
In hog options, Kasa actively bought the June 83 call early, seen as short covering, traders said.

Cargill Investor Services bought October 74 puts while R.J. O'Brien sold June 88 calls. Commission houses sold June 84 and 86 calls early. Volatility was firm, 18 to 21 percent in June on back, pit sources added.
The strong tone to cash bellies continued to support pork belly futures with late fund buying adding to support and offsetting local selling interest and light profit taking, traders said.

Prices on cash bellies, weighing 14-16 lbs, rose to the highest level since late January at $76.50 per cwt and expectations are for values to rise above $77 soon. This would put cash at its highest level since early October, 1996, they said.
The lack of a hedge in futures was also supportive as there was no encouragement to store product needed for the approaching peak demand season, some sources noted.
"Futures are too low to give you a hedge," said Julia Bussie, analyst for AG Edwards.
Smith Barney and LIT division of First Options bought late. R.J. O'Brien and Rand Financials were early buyers, pit sources said.
